title: Two marriages and the difficulty of musicians' home life
summary: He first married in St. Paul in the early 1930s, a marriage lasting seven years, and a second that was on the rocks; he could never settle down.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Now had you married at this point, yet?
Yes, I first married when I was with Alabamians, Hardy's Alabamians, then that's when I got -- when I first married.
I see and that -- so that was in the early '30's.
St. Paul, Minnesota.
Yes.
St. Paul, Minnesota.
In St. Paul?
Uh-huh.
And when was that -- in the '30's, early '30's?
Early '30's, yes.
Yeah.
Well that lasted seven years.
Uh-huh. So that when you went on vacation to Paris, in '39, you were no longer married?
That's right. Now wait a minute, '30, to
'37, I was married, then I was -- I married a second time and when I went on the vacation to Paris, I was married the second time, but it was on the rocks, also.
I see.

Because I could never buckle down to being married. You know, because it's very difficult for a musician -- during that time and even now, to settle down to married life. That's when you're going here and going there. It's very hard because you can't -- you don't have time for home life.
Right.

I mean I couldn't -- now some musicians could do that, but I didn't have time to settle down and say well I'm a married man, I've got to be home right after -- I got to do this, I got to do that, I could never buckle down to that.
You need a very understanding wife, I guess.
Yes, and I don't think there were very many around during that time.
